params.body:
Third of three, and the one that was actually the point. "Da's een beetje flauwe analytics hè" — it was, and the reason was structural rather than cosmetic.

The tab showed eight measures each once, in a stack of collapsible sections I had copied from the Werking screen. That is a status layout: built to be scanned on a quiet morning to see whether anything is wrong. It is not built to be asked a question. You could read that Thursday is the busiest day and had no way to ask busy with what, by whom, or compared to when — while the data for all three was already sitting there.

## One measure, sliced many ways

The reader picks the measure — handlings, edits, views, sign-ins — and every cut on the page follows it: over time, per weekday, per hour, per garage. `?maat=` in the url, next to `?periode=`, so a question is a link.

That inversion is the whole change. "Edits per weekday" went from unaskable to one click.

## The comparison is the headline, not a grey footnote

The big number on the screen is now the **difference** against the previous period of the same length. The total stands underneath it. A count on its own does not say whether anything changed, and whether anything changed is the only question the screen exists for.

## Three things it now refuses to imply

- **The running step is marked as running.** Today, or this month, is drawn faded and says so. Without it this morning reads as a collapse every morning — which is exactly what it did at half past three last night, and what prompted this.
- **A measure is not compared against a period it was not being measured in.** The event log and the page counter started this week; over a twelve-month window they would show a catastrophic drop that never happened. The comparison comes back empty and the screen says why.
- **Views know no hour.** They are a daily total, so the hour chart is absent for that measure with a line saying so, rather than drawn empty and read as "nobody works".

## Who carries it

The garage list now shows each one's **share** of the measure. Eight garages carrying half the platform is a different fact from eighty carrying it evenly, and a column of numbers does not show that.

## Verified

`OneMeasureSlicedManyWaysTest`: every measure answers every cut (as a data provider over all four, so a fifth cannot be added without answering them too), the running step is marked and only the last one, a measure is not compared with a period it did not exist in, the page counter is summed rather than counted, a daily total knows no hour, an unknown measure falls back, and each measure and window has its own cache key so switching never serves the previous answer.

The event-log test moved with the screen: the start date used to live in its own block and now sits with the measure it belongs to, which is where a reader needs it.

`phpstan` green over the project, `pint` green on the touched files. Local suite: the same nine failures as on a clean `main` in my environment (two known `ListPageHeadersTest`, six `IntegrationSmokeTest` reading an `OUTBOUND_IMPACT` from my local `.env`, one warranty test). CI runs on a fresh database.

New rule R P3-16.11.

## Still not in it

Drill-down from a number to the rows behind it — click a garage, see what they did. Inzichten can do that and this cannot yet. It needs its own endpoint and panel, and it is a better change once somebody has used this for a week and can say which number they wanted to open.

The charts on the other tab are still Bootstrap while this one is Tailwind. That conversion stays a separate, bounded job.
params.title: One measure, sliced many ways
